newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Thursday due to renewed market talk that the central bank would shortly cut bank reserve ratios, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract plunged to 3.58 percent from Wednesday's 7.5 percent.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell slightly to 1.81 million lots from 1.88 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said Thursday's trading was dominated by renewed market rumours that the central bank, the People's Bank of China, was planning to cut bank reserve ratios. The rumours have circulated on the market time and again since late last year.
Central bank officials have declined to comment.
"The talk made most institutions, including securities houses, stay on the sidelines today and that was what pushed down the repo rates," one trader said.
One firm had planned to issue 55 million domestic A shares on the Shenzhen exchange on Friday but the issue was delayed to Monday, reducing the repo market's fund demand, traders said.
"Lending by big institutions pushed down the repo contracts, in particular the three-day contract," a second trader said.
Traders said they believed the rates would move around at the current low levels on Friday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday with the rumours of a bank reserve ratio cut boosting market sentiment, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 112.18 yuan from 112.12 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 807,370 lots from 1.4 million lots.
Traders said investors believed a cut in bank reserve ratios would add cash supply to the spot market.
"This helped boost market sentiment today," a trader said.
Traders said they expected the contracts to continue to rise on Friday, albeit slightly.
